assessment: R-04-06 uses PD for pancreaticoduodenectomy in postoperative risk assessment.
R-07-02 describes PTEG in 23 patients, including two with Parkinson disease. Technical results are pooled and no food was reported.
R-07-04 documents recovery during withdrawal of a suspected drug and combined feeding support in drug-induced parkinsonism. Individual foods and separate effects are unreported.
O-01-07 studies PD-L1 expression in an immune checkpoint inhibitor study.
O-10-07 measures PD-1 and PD-L1 expression in esophageal cancer cells after HMB and other exposures.
O-12-04 analyzes weight loss after pancreaticoduodenectomy.
O-16-03 compares 27 new PSP cases with the previously reported 31 Parkinson cases after gastrostomy. No named food or new Parkinson exposure was analyzed.
O-16-05 uses PD for Faith phylogenetic diversity in stroke rehabilitation.
O-32-04 uses PD for partially degraded bone microarchitecture.
O-33-04 lists Parkinson drugs as possible pressure-injury risk exposures in a prescription study.
O-33-08 describes collagen peptides, zinc and later MCT oil alongside changing energy, protein and wound care. No isolated oil or Parkinson symptom result.
O-34-06 reports a persistent PTEG tract after tube removal in a 90-year-old with Parkinson disease and prior reflux and aspiration. The resumed oral diet has no named foods.

O-35-06 reports a bezoar on viscosity-changing formula, small shrinkage after carbonated water lavage and resolution after digestive enzymes. The case does not measure swallowing with carbonated water.
P-06-02 describes pancreaticoduodenectomy followed by COVID-19 and taste impairment, with perioperative nutrition support and zinc. PD denotes the surgical procedure.

P-17-02 uses PD for planned pancreaticoduodenectomy in an 80-year-old with pancreatic/duodenal tumor and sarcopenia. He instead received a gastric-jejunal bypass, followed by advancing textures, oral nutrition and whole rice porridge.
P-17-03 compares nutritional indices and postoperative length of stay before and after a team was set up for pancreaticoduodenectomy. PD denotes surgery.

P-26-01 describes a man in his 80s with stage 3 Parkinson disease, polytrauma and subsequent stroke. Soft rice and soft side dishes were advanced to a regular diet, with unnamed supplementary formula and intensive rehabilitation. Weight increased 46.3 to 50.2 kg and FIM 42 to 95. No specific swallowing or preparation effect was measured.

P-31-03 reports severe hypoglycemia in 32 of 106 deceased Utano Parkinson patients from January 2006 through March 2024, matching the Parkinson sample and count at 2024 NHO. Lowest glucose group means were 27.3 versus 67.9 mg/dL. Low albumin, high CRP and AST above 60 were independently associated. Seven of nine measured severe cases had insulin at or below 0.4 microunits/mL. Nine of 17 severe cases with liver injury recovered during nutritional supplementation. No specific food was named.

P-31-04 followed 54 Utano inpatients prospectively, including 39 with Parkinson disease or dementia with Lewy bodies combined. Eighteen received airway suction and five had an event defined by oxygen saturation falling to 90% or below then recovering to 90% or above with suction. Neck extension was associated with events (p=.02). The poster gives neither food or meal timing nor a Parkinson-specific event count.

P-33-04 used an unspecified oral swallowing-training jelly together with tube and parenteral feeding in an 80-year-old man with Parkinson dysphagia and 18% weight loss over seven months. Tube feeding was held on day 3 for suspected aspiration pneumonia. The abstract does not attribute this to the jelly or report a preparation-specific result.

P-33-10 describes an older woman with parkinsonism, vascular dementia and secondary normal-pressure hydrocephalus who developed shock after escalation of gastrostomy feeding, diagnosed as refeeding syndrome. Later formulations are described by caloric concentration only. No oral food or ingredient-specific Parkinson outcome.

P-50-03 describes a man in his 70s with parkinsonism and Alzheimer dementia, taste complaints and polypharmacy. Chopped meals with whole rice porridge resumed on day 20. He declined supplemental food. Serum zinc rose from 61 to 85 micrograms/dL and intake reached about 80% after oral zinc acetate 50 mg amid other care. No ingredient-specific taste outcome or idiopathic Parkinson diagnosis.

P-50-06 reports medium rice porridge and Ensure H in a woman with Parkinson disease, depression, deep vein thrombosis and preadmission visual hallucinations. She finished meals and could feed herself by day 39 after concurrent medication, rehabilitation, psychological and nutrition interventions. No isolated effect of Ensure H or rice or item-level hallucination follow-up.
P-51-10 studies skeletal muscle index and prognosis in 89 older pancreatic cancer patients receiving pancreaticoduodenectomy. PD denotes surgery.

P-59-01 is a within-person texture sequence in an 84-year-old man with Parkinson disease and obstructing sigmoid colon cancer. WBC and CRP rose mildly when blended rice porridge was advanced to soft rice porridge and improved on return to blended porridge. No fever or oxygen saturation fall accompanied the change. The authors suspected microaspiration without an instrumental confirmation or reported choking event. Rice textures and concurrent tube feeding, no baked potato.

P-60-02 reports a Japanese anticholinergic risk checklist in 16 nutrition support cases. One anticholinergic was a Parkinson medication, with no separate disease diagnosis or directly attributed dysphagia among the reviewed medication-change cases. No food exposure.

P-63-01 reports an 87-year-old woman with Parkinson disease, prior lacunar infarct and aspiration pneumonia. Swallowing endoscopy score improved from 8 to 5 after intravenous levodopa improved alertness and training progressed. Unspecified medication-assistance jelly helped tablet administration. No isolated jelly or food effect.

P-69-04 reports an autistic four-year-old girl with a restricted diet of mainly fried potato and barley tea and micronutrient deficiencies, evaluated for bilateral Bartholin gland abscess. No Parkinson diagnosis, baked preparation or choking outcome.

P-71-08 describes an 86-year-old woman with Parkinson disease who resumed tube nutrition via a W-ED device while receiving drainage and antibiotics for infected gastrostomy site. No formula, oral food, or symptom-specific analysis.

P-73-03 describes an 80-year-old woman with parkinsonism-related dysphagia undergoing surgery for gastrostomy-related gastrocolocutaneous fistula. Unnamed tube feed restarted on postoperative day 3. No oral food or Parkinson-specific effect.
P-75-05 describes esophageal cancer progression after chemotherapy and multiple enteral products used during later surgical complications. PD denotes progressive disease.

P-76-05 reports a 77-year-old man with Parkinson disease and cognitive impairment recovering from severe burns. Videofluoroscopy found no oral or pharyngeal phase deficit. Gastrostomy feeding and rehabilitation were intensified, oral lunch resumed and weight increased from 39.3 to 45.8 kg at four months. No specified ingredient or isolated Parkinson symptom effect.
